clues: I was formed from the dust of the ground.
God placed me in a garden to tend and keep it.
I was given the task of naming every living creature.
My rib was taken to form my companion.
I am remembered as the very first man.
I was made to be a companion for the first man.
A cunning serpent spoke to me in the garden.
I was persuaded to eat fruit from a forbidden tree.
I shared that fruit with my husband.
I am called the mother of all the living.
In a world grown violent and corrupt, I found favor with God.
I spent years building a massive vessel on dry land.
I brought pairs of animals aboard to survive a coming flood.
My family and I floated safely while the earth was covered in water.
God set a rainbow in the sky as a promise to me.
God called me to leave my homeland for a place I had never seen.
I was promised descendants as countless as the stars.
My wife and I waited decades for the son we were promised.
I was tested when asked to offer my son on a mountain.
I am honored as the father of many nations.
As a baby, I was hidden in a basket among river reeds.
I fled to the desert after a violent act caught up with me.
God spoke to me from a bush that burned but was not consumed.
I confronted a powerful king and demanded freedom for my people.
I brought down two stone tablets from a mountain.
I was the youngest of my brothers, out watching sheep.
A giant mocked my people, so I faced him with only a sling.
My music once calmed a troubled king's spirit.
I was anointed king long before I actually took the throne.
Many of the Psalms are credited to me.
Offered anything I wanted, I asked God for wisdom.
Two women once brought a disputed baby before me for judgment.
I oversaw the building of a magnificent temple.
My wealth and wisdom drew visitors from distant lands.
I was the son who inherited my father David's throne.
My birth was announced by an angel before I arrived.
I began teaching and healing around the age of thirty.
I taught crowds using simple stories with deep meaning.
I was crucified, and my followers found my tomb empty three days later.
I am called the Son of God and the Savior of the world.
An angel visited me with news that changed everything.
I was engaged when I learned I would bear a special son.
I gave birth far from home because there was no room for us.
I stood near a cross, watching my son suffer.
I am remembered as the mother of Jesus.
I left my fishing nets behind to follow a new teacher.
I once stepped out of a boat and walked on water, briefly.
I denied knowing my teacher three times in a single night.
I preached boldly on the day the Holy Spirit came in power.
I am usually named first among the twelve apostles.
My brothers resented the special coat my father gave me.
I was sold into slavery by my own family.
I correctly interpreted troubling dreams for a king.
I rose from a prison cell to become second in command of Egypt.
I eventually forgave the brothers who betrayed me.
I gripped my twin brother's heel as we were born.
I tricked my father into giving me a blessing meant for my brother.
I wrestled with a mysterious figure through the night.
My name was changed after that struggle.
My twelve sons became the twelve tribes of Israel.
My birth to elderly parents was a fulfillment of God's promise.
As a boy, I nearly became a sacrifice on a mountain altar.
A wife was found for me through a servant's prayerful search.
My wife struggled to conceive until my prayers were answered.
I was Abraham's long-awaited son.
I laughed when I overheard a promise that seemed impossible for my old age.
I struggled for years with the pain of not having children.
I gave my servant to my husband, hoping for a child that way.
I finally gave birth to the son God had promised.
I am remembered as the mother of Isaac.
My great strength was tied to a vow made before my birth.
I once tore apart a lion with my bare hands.
I fell in love with a woman who betrayed my secret.
My hair was cut, and my strength left me.
I brought down a temple with my final burst of strength.
I was one of only two spies who trusted God's promise about the land.
I took over leadership after a great prophet's death.
I led my people across a river on dry ground.
City walls fell after my people marched around them.
I divided the promised land among the tribes.
I was not born among God's people, but I chose to stay with my mother-in-law.
I gleaned leftover grain in the fields to survive.
A kind landowner noticed my loyalty and provided for me.
I married the man who became my family's redeemer.
I became an ancestor of King David.
I hid my identity when I was chosen for a royal position.
My cousin raised me and warned me of danger to our people.
I risked my life by approaching the king uninvited.
I exposed a plot to destroy my people.
A feast still celebrates the deliverance I helped bring about.
I refused to eat food that would defile me at a foreign court.
I could interpret dreams and mysterious visions.
Jealous officials tricked a king into signing a law aimed at me.
I was thrown into a den of lions for my faithfulness.
I survived the night, unharmed, among the lions.
I lived in the wilderness, wearing camel's hair and eating wild food.
I called people to turn from wrongdoing and be washed clean.
I baptized my own cousin in a river.
I said I must decrease while he must increase.
My outspokenness against a king's marriage cost me my head.
I tried to run away from what God asked me to do.
I boarded a ship heading the opposite direction.
A great storm arose because of me.
I spent three days and nights inside a great fish.
I eventually preached to a city I didn't want to see saved.
I challenged hundreds of false prophets to a contest of fire.
Ravens brought me food while I hid by a brook.
A widow's flour and oil never ran out while I stayed with her.
I fled in fear after a queen threatened my life.
I was taken up to heaven in a whirlwind, in a chariot of fire.
I received a double portion of my mentor's spirit.
I watched my teacher taken up into heaven.
I helped a poor widow's jar of oil keep flowing.
I told a foreign commander to wash seven times in a river to be healed.
I succeeded a prophet who was taken up in a whirlwind.
I was threshing wheat in hiding when an angel called me a mighty warrior.
I asked for signs with wool and dew before trusting my mission.
I reduced my army from thousands to just a few hundred.
My men carried torches hidden inside jars into battle.
I delivered my people from oppressors with an unusual, tiny army.
I served my people as a judge, sitting under a palm tree.
I sent for a military commander and told him God's battle plan.
I went with him to the battlefield when he hesitated to go alone.
A song of victory is recorded in my honor and words.
I am remembered as a rare woman judge of Israel.
I was described as blameless and upright, a man of great wealth.
I lost my children, my possessions, and my health in a single trial.
My friends offered explanations for my suffering that missed the truth.
I questioned God directly about my pain.
My fortunes were restored twofold after my trial ended.
I once persecuted the very people I would later lead.
A blinding light stopped me on a road to a city called Damascus.
I traveled extensively, planting churches across the region.
I wrote many letters that became part of the New Testament.
I was once named Saul before my dramatic change of heart.
I carried the money bag for our group.
I struck a deal for a small sum of silver.
I identified my teacher to his enemies with a kiss.
Remorse overwhelmed me after I saw what I had done.
My name has become a byword for betrayal.
I was delivered from a deeply troubled past.
I followed and supported a traveling teacher and his followers.
I stood near the cross when most others had fled.
I came early to a tomb, expecting to find a body.
I was the first to see him alive again and told the others.
I was not present the first time my risen teacher appeared to the others.
I said I would not believe without seeing the wounds myself.
I was invited to touch the very marks I doubted.
My doubt turned instantly into a confession of faith.
My name is now linked forever with skepticism.
I served as a spokesman for a family member who struggled to speak.
I carried a staff that budded overnight as a sign of God's choosing.
I fashioned a golden idol under pressure from an impatient crowd.
I was set apart as the first high priest of my people.
I was Moses' older brother.
I watched over my baby brother as he floated in a basket.
I led the women in song and dance after a miraculous crossing.
I questioned my younger brother's authority alongside another sibling.
I was struck with a skin disease as a consequence.
I am remembered as a prophetess and the sister of Moses and Aaron.
I offered water to a stranger's camels at a well, unaware it was a test.
A servant's prayer led him straight to me as a bride for his master's son.
I struggled with twins wrestling inside me before they were even born.
I favored one son and helped him deceive his father for a blessing.
I became the wife of Isaac.
I hid enemy spies on my roof under stalks of flax.
I tied a scarlet cord in my window as a sign of protection.
My household was the only one spared when the city walls fell.
I left my old life behind and joined the people of Israel.
I became an ancestor in the line leading to King David.
As a child, I heard my name called in the night and mistook it for my mentor's voice.
I served in the tabernacle from a very young age.
I anointed the first king my people ever had.
I later anointed a shepherd boy who would replace that king.
I am remembered as a judge, priest, and prophet.
I stood head and shoulders above my people when chosen as their first king.
I was anointed by a prophet while searching for lost donkeys.
Jealousy over a young warrior's fame consumed me.
I hurled a spear at the very man I once loved like a son.
My reign ended in defeat on a mountain battlefield.
I served as a cupbearer in a foreign king's palace.
News of my homeland's broken walls brought me to tears.
I was granted permission to return and rebuild what was ruined.
I organized workers who built with a tool in one hand and a weapon in the other.
I completed the wall despite fierce opposition.
I was a scribe devoted to studying and teaching the Law.
I led a group of exiles back to my homeland.
I tore my clothes in grief over my people's unfaithfulness.
I read the Law aloud to a gathered crowd for hours.
I helped restore proper worship after the exile.
I was a respected religious leader among my people.
I came to speak with a teacher under cover of night.
I was told I must be born again, and I didn't understand at first.
I later defended that same teacher before hostile colleagues.
I helped prepare his body for burial with costly spices.
I collected taxes for a foreign empire, and I was not well-liked for it.
I was too short to see over the crowd.
I climbed a tree just to catch a glimpse of a passing teacher.
I was surprised to be invited down and welcomed by name.
I promised to repay anyone I had cheated four times over.
I owned fields where a foreign widow came to gather leftover grain.
I instructed my workers to leave extra grain behind for her.
I noticed her loyalty and kindness to her mother-in-law.
I fulfilled the role of a family redeemer for her.
I became the great-grandfather of King David.
Famine drove my family from our homeland to a foreign country.
I lost my husband and both my sons while abroad.
I urged my daughters-in-law to return to their own people.
One of them refused to leave my side.
I returned home bitter, but was later comforted by a grandson.
A king saw me bathing from his rooftop.
My husband was sent to the front lines to die because of that king's desire for me.
I lost the child born from that affair.
I later became the mother of Israel's wisest king.
A prophet confronted the king over what happened to me and my husband.
I avenged my sister's mistreatment by killing my own brother.
I spent years in exile before being welcomed back to court.
I stood at the city gate, winning the hearts of the people.
I led a rebellion against my own father, the king.
My long hair caught in a tree branch during my final battle.
I brought foreign gods into my husband's kingdom.
I hunted down prophets who opposed my religion.
I arranged false charges to seize a vineyard I wanted.
A prophet fled for his life after I threatened him.
My name became a symbol of wickedness and manipulation.
I saw a vision of God's throne, surrounded by heavenly beings.
I cried out that I was a man of unclean lips.
A coal touched my lips to cleanse me before I was sent.
I prophesied both judgment and comfort to my people.
My writings include famous predictions about a coming servant and Messiah.
I protested that I was too young when I was called.
I wept over the coming destruction of my beloved city.
I was thrown into a muddy cistern for my unpopular warnings.
I wrote laments mourning my nation's downfall.
I am remembered as the weeping prophet.
I saw a vision of wheels within wheels and strange living creatures.
I was struck mute for a season as a sign to my people.
I acted out prophecies through strange, symbolic behavior.
I saw a valley filled with dry bones come back to life.
I prophesied to exiles far from their homeland.
My sisters sent word that I was gravely ill.
I died before help arrived, and I was buried in a tomb.
I had been dead four days when a stone was rolled away.
A loud command called me back out, still wrapped in grave clothes.
My return to life became one of the most talked-about miracles.
I welcomed a traveling teacher into my home.
I busied myself with preparations while my sister sat listening.
I complained that I had been left to serve alone.
I professed my faith even while grieving my brother's death.
I was the sister of Mary and Lazarus.
I was one of twelve sent to scout out a promised land.
Unlike most of my companions, I brought back a hopeful report.
I remained faithful through decades of wilderness wandering.
At eighty-five, I still asked for a mountain to conquer.
I entered the promised land alongside Joshua, unlike my generation.
I was driven away by my own family because of my mother's status.
Desperate leaders eventually came asking me to lead them in battle.
I made a rash vow before going to war.
My own daughter was the first to greet me on my return.
I am remembered among the judges who delivered Israel.
A prophetess summoned me with a battle plan from God.
I refused to go into battle without her by my side.
Because of my hesitation, the glory of victory went to another woman instead.
I led ten thousand men down from a mountain to face an iron-chariot army.
I am listed among the judges and among the faithful in Hebrews.
I was deeply troubled by my inability to have children.
A priest mistook my silent, desperate prayer for drunkenness.
I vowed to dedicate my son to God's service if given one.
I brought my young son to live at the tabernacle after he was weaned.
My song of praise echoes themes later found in Mary's own song.
I served as high priest and judge in a troubled era.
I raised a boy who had been dedicated to serve alongside me.
My own sons dishonored their priestly duties.
I failed to restrain their wrongdoing despite warnings.
News of a lost sacred chest and my sons' deaths caused my own fatal fall.
I served as a prophet during a king's reign.
I told a king a story about a poor man's beloved lamb.
My story was a trap that exposed the king's own sin.
I declared to the king, 'You are the man.'
I later helped ensure Solomon, not a rival, took the throne.
I removed idols and restored proper worship in my kingdom.
I tore my clothes upon hearing a mocking, threatening letter.
I wept and prayed when told I would soon die.
My life was extended by fifteen years after that prayer.
I commissioned a tunnel to secure my city's water supply.
I became king while still just a boy.
A long-lost scroll of the Law was discovered during my reign.
I tore my robes upon hearing what it said.
I led a sweeping reform, destroying idols across the land.
I renewed my people's covenant with God.
I was chosen to help distribute food fairly among widows.
I performed wonders and spoke with unusual wisdom.
I delivered a bold speech before a hostile religious council.
I saw a vision of heaven opened just before my death.
I became the first martyr of the early church, stoned for my faith.
My name means 'son of encouragement.'
I sold a field and gave the proceeds to the early believers.
I vouched for a former persecutor when others feared him.
I traveled alongside that same man on missionary journeys.
I later split from him over a disagreement about a young companion.
I was both a king and a priest, a rare combination.
I brought out bread and wine to a returning warrior.
I blessed him, and he gave me a tenth of everything.
My priesthood is described as having no recorded beginning or end.
A New Testament book compares a greater priest to my order.
I was a priest in a foreign land where a fugitive found refuge.
I gave my daughter in marriage to that fugitive.
I later visited him after he led a great deliverance.
I advised him to appoint capable leaders to share his burden.
I was the father-in-law of Moses.
A foreign king hired me to curse an approaching nation.
My own donkey saw an angel before I did.
My donkey spoke to me after I struck it in frustration.
I could only speak the blessings God put in my mouth.
Despite my failed curses, I later led that nation into sin.
I captured a city and won a bride as my reward.
I am named as the very first judge to deliver my people.
The Spirit came upon me before I went to war.
I brought decades of peace after my victory.
I was the nephew of Caleb.
I was left-handed, which helped hide my weapon.
I strapped a hidden blade to my right thigh.
I told a foreign king I had a secret message for him alone.
I delivered that message with my concealed weapon instead of words.
I delivered my people from oppression after that encounter.
I was a king's daughter who fell in love with a rising warrior.
I helped my husband escape through a window when my father sought his life.
I was later given to another man while my husband was in exile.
I watched my husband dance before the ark with great abandon.
I despised him for it, and we grew estranged.
I was heir to my father's throne, yet I supported another man's rise instead.
I made a covenant of friendship with my father's rival.
I warned my friend of my father's murderous intentions.
I once attacked an enemy garrison with just my armor-bearer.
I died alongside my father in the same battle.
I was one of my king's mighty warriors.
My wife caught the king's eye while I was away at war.
I refused to go home and enjoy comfort while my fellow soldiers camped in the field.
I unknowingly carried the letter that sealed my own fate.
I was placed on the front line and abandoned there to die.
I raised my orphaned cousin as my own daughter.
I refused to bow to an arrogant official.
That refusal led to a plot against my entire people.
I uncovered an assassination plot and reported it, unrewarded at first.
I was honored publicly by the very enemy who plotted my death.
I was promoted to the highest position in the king's court.
I was enraged when one man refused to bow to me.
I plotted to destroy an entire people over that one insult.
I built gallows intended for my enemy.
I was hanged on the very structure I built for another.
I cursed a fleeing king and threw stones and dust at him.
I claimed loyalty once that same king was restored to power.
I was spared for a time despite my earlier hostility.
I was warned never to leave the city under threat of death.
I broke that condition years later and paid the price.
I was once a trusted counselor whose advice was like consulting God himself.
I abandoned my king to join a rebellion led by his own son.
My counsel was rejected in favor of a rival advisor's plan.
I saw that the rebellion would fail because of that rejection.
I put my affairs in order and ended my own life.
I was a king's daughter, known for my beauty.
My own half-brother deceived and violated me.
I tore my royal robe and mourned openly afterward.
My full brother avenged me two years later.
My story reveals the painful consequences within a royal family.
I was a concubine caught in the aftermath of a royal power struggle.
My sons were handed over and executed to end a famine.
I guarded their exposed bodies from birds and beasts for months.
My devotion moved a king to finally give proper burial to the dead.
My vigil is remembered as an act of fierce, sorrowful loyalty.
I served as a servant to a prophet with a powerful ministry.
A foreign commander was healed of a skin disease through my master.
I secretly chased after that commander for gifts my master refused.
I lied about where I had been.
The disease my master refused to profit from clung to me instead.
I commanded an army for a foreign king, though I suffered from a skin disease.
A captive servant girl told my wife of a prophet who could heal me.
I was offended when told to simply wash in a river seven times.
My servants convinced me to swallow my pride and try it anyway.
I was healed and declared there was no God like the one I had found.
My name means 'servant of the Lord.'
I wrote the shortest book among the Old Testament prophets.
My message was directed against a neighboring nation related by blood.
I condemned that nation for gloating over my people's downfall.
I promised that deliverance and justice would ultimately prevail.
I questioned God openly about why evil seemed to go unpunished.
I was troubled by the answer, which involved an even more violent nation.
I stationed myself on a watchtower, waiting for God's reply.
I wrote that the righteous will live by faith.
My book ends with a song of trust despite hardship.
I was a prophetess consulted about a newly discovered scroll.
A king's officials sought me out for guidance during a religious reform.
I confirmed that the words of the scroll would surely come to pass.
I foretold both coming judgment and mercy for a repentant king.
My counsel was trusted even by the king's own advisors.
I seized the throne after my son the king was killed.
I tried to destroy the entire royal line to secure my power.
One infant was secretly hidden from my purge.
That hidden child was revealed years later as the rightful king.
I was executed once my usurped reign was exposed.
I was anointed king in secret while serving as a military commander.
I drove my chariot furiously, recognized from a distance by my driving.
I carried out God's judgment against a corrupt royal house.
I orchestrated the death of a notorious queen.
Despite my zeal, my own dynasty later fell short of full faithfulness.
I traced my lineage back several generations in my own book's opening.
I warned of a coming day of God's wrath.
I condemned complacency among my people.
I prophesied judgment on surrounding nations as well as my own.
I closed my book with a promise of joyful restoration.
I prophesied the downfall of a great and cruel city.
That city had earlier repented under another prophet's warning, but returned to evil.
I described God as slow to anger but not one who leaves the guilty unpunished.
My vivid poetry described chariots racing through the streets in judgment.
My short book focuses entirely on one doomed empire's capital.
I am considered the final voice among the Old Testament prophets.
I confronted priests for offering blemished sacrifices.
I rebuked my people for withholding their tithes.
I promised a messenger would come to prepare the way before the Lord.
My name means 'my messenger.'
I was chosen to help distribute food, alongside another future martyr.
I explained scripture to a traveling official from a distant land.
I baptized that official beside the road after their conversation.
I was suddenly carried away by the Spirit after that encounter.
I later hosted an apostle and had four daughters who prophesied.
I collected taxes before I was called to follow a new teacher.
I hosted a large dinner for my teacher and many like myself.
Religious leaders criticized my teacher for eating with people like me.
I am also known by another name, Levi.
A Gospel bearing my name opens the New Testament.
I belonged to a group fiercely opposed to foreign rule.
I was one of the twelve closest followers of Jesus.
Little is recorded about me individually in the Gospels.
My background contrasted sharply with a tax collector among the twelve.
I am mentioned mainly in the lists naming the apostles.
I was a fisherman alongside my more famous brother.
I had first followed John the Baptist before changing teachers.
I was the one who brought my brother to meet Jesus.
I pointed out a boy with a few loaves and fish before a miracle.
I am remembered as one of the first disciples called.
I was a fisherman, the son of Zebedee.
My brother and I were nicknamed 'sons of thunder.'
I was part of an inner circle present at key private moments.
My mother once asked for me to sit at a place of honor.
I became the first apostle martyred for the faith.
I was a fisherman, brother to another apostle.
I am often described as the disciple whom Jesus loved.
I leaned close to Jesus at the Last Supper.
I was entrusted with the care of Jesus' mother.
I am traditionally credited with writing a Gospel and a vivid book of visions.
I ran away from the man I served.
I crossed paths with an imprisoned apostle who became like a father to me.
That apostle sent me back to the man I had wronged.
A short New Testament letter pleads on my behalf.
My name means 'useful,' a play on words in that very letter.
I was sent by a church to deliver a gift to an imprisoned apostle.
I became seriously ill, nearly to the point of death, during my service.
The apostle called me his brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier.
I was anxious about how my home church would react to news of my illness.
I am mentioned by name in a letter to the Philippians.
I carried letters on behalf of an imprisoned apostle to distant churches.
I am described as a beloved brother and faithful servant.
I was sent to encourage hearts with news of the apostle's situation.
I appear in multiple New Testament letters as a trusted courier.
I was entrusted with delivering both personal and church-wide news.
My husband and I worked as tentmakers alongside a traveling apostle.
We hosted a church that met in our own home.
We took aside a gifted, eloquent speaker to explain the faith more accurately to him.
I am often named before my husband in the New Testament, unusual for the time.
We are remembered as a devoted ministry couple.
My wife and I were forced to leave Rome due to an imperial decree.
I shared a trade with a well-known apostle who stayed and worked with us.
We hosted a church in our home in more than one city.
We helped instruct a gifted preacher more accurately in the faith.
I am almost always mentioned together with my wife.
I was an eloquent speaker with a thorough knowledge of the scriptures.
I taught boldly but only knew part of the story at first.
A ministry couple took me aside to explain things more accurately.
I went on to powerfully refute opponents in public debate.
Some believers in Corinth favored my teaching over others', causing division.
I was a leader among the early believers, chosen to deliver an important letter.
I accompanied an apostle on missionary travels after an earlier partner departed.
I was flogged and imprisoned alongside that apostle in one city.
We sang hymns in our cell, and an earthquake shook the prison doors open.
I later helped write at least one New Testament letter.
My mother and grandmother had a faith that was passed down to me.
An apostle became like a spiritual father to me.
I was left in charge of a church despite my relative youth.
I was urged not to let anyone look down on me for my age.
Two New Testament letters are addressed directly to me.
I was a Gentile companion of an apostle on his travels.
I was left behind on an island to organize the church there.
I was instructed to appoint elders in every town.
I helped deliver a difficult letter to a troubled church.
A New Testament letter bears my name.
A church met in my own home.
My runaway servant crossed paths with an imprisoned apostle.
That apostle sent my servant back to me with a personal appeal.
I was urged to receive him back as a brother, not merely a servant.
A short New Testament letter is addressed directly to me.
I worked the ground as a tiller of the soil.
My offering of the fruit of the ground was not respected by God.
God warned me that sin was lying at the door.
I asked God, "Am I my brother's keeper?"
I killed my brother Abel, and God set a mark upon me.
I was a keeper of sheep.
I brought the firstlings of my flock as an offering.
God had respect unto me and to my offering.
My blood cried out to God from the ground.
I was Adam and Eve's second son, killed by my older brother.
My mother said God had appointed me in place of a son who was slain.
In my son Enos's days, men began to call upon the name of the LORD.
My father was 130 years old when I was born.
I was born in my father's likeness, after his image.
I was the son born to Adam and Eve after Abel's death.
My son lived longer than any other man recorded.
I lived 365 years on the earth.
Jude records my prophecy that the Lord comes with ten thousands of his saints.
I walked with God.
I was translated so that I should not see death, for God took me.
My son was named Lamech.
Noah was my grandson.
My father walked with God.
My father was taken by God without dying.
I lived 969 years, longer than anyone else recorded.
I travelled from Haran with my uncle.
Our herdsmen quarrelled, so my uncle and I parted ways.
I chose the well-watered plain of Jordan and pitched my tent toward Sodom.
Two angels urged me to flee the city before it was destroyed.
My wife looked back and became a pillar of salt.
An angel named me before I was born.
It was said I would be a wild man, my hand against every man.
I was seen mocking at a feast, and my mother and I were sent away.
God heard my voice as I lay under a shrub in the wilderness.
I was Abraham's son by Hagar.
I was an Egyptian handmaid.
I fled from my mistress into the wilderness.
I called the LORD "Thou God seest me."
God opened my eyes to see a well of water in the wilderness of Beersheba.
I bore Ishmael to Abraham.
I was a cunning hunter, a man of the field.
I was born red, hairy all over like a garment.
I sold my birthright for a meal of red pottage.
My brother took our father's blessing by wearing goatskins on his hands.
I was Jacob's twin brother.
I ran out to meet Abraham's servant at the well.
My sister Rebekah left home to marry Isaac.
My nephew said I changed his wages ten times.
My daughter stole my household gods.
I gave Leah to Jacob in place of Rachel.
I was a shepherdess who came to the well with my father's sheep.
A man served seven years for me, and they seemed but a few days.
I hid my father's images in the camel's furniture and sat upon them.
I died giving birth on the way to Bethlehem.
I was Jacob's beloved wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin.
My eyes were described as tender.
I was given in marriage in place of my younger sister.
I named a son Judah, saying, "Now will I praise the LORD."
I was buried in the cave of Machpelah.
I was Laban's elder daughter and Jacob's first wife.
I found mandrakes in the field and brought them to my mother.
I persuaded my brothers not to kill our brother, but to cast him into a pit.
I returned to the pit and tore my clothes when the boy was gone.
My father said I was unstable as water.
I was Jacob's firstborn son.
I suggested selling our brother to the Ishmeelites instead of killing him.
My daughter-in-law Tamar disguised herself, and I did not know her.
I offered to stay as a slave in place of my youngest brother.
My father said the sceptre would not depart from me.
I was Jacob's fourth son, by Leah; a tribe and a kingdom bear my name.
My dying mother named me Benoni.
My father renamed me with a name meaning "son of the right hand."
At a feast my portion was five times as much as my brothers'.
A silver cup was found in my sack.
I was the youngest son of Jacob and Rachel.
I am the one daughter named among Jacob's children.
I went out to see the daughters of the land.
Shechem the son of Hamor took me and defiled me.
My brothers Simeon and Levi avenged me with the sword.
My mother was Leah.
I was an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard.
I bought a Hebrew slave from the Ishmeelites.
I saw that the LORD made all my servant did to prosper.
My wife accused my servant falsely.
I put Joseph into the prison where the king's prisoners were bound.
I was born in Egypt; my mother was Asenath.
My name was chosen because God had made my father fruitful in the land of affliction.
My grandfather crossed his hands to bless me.
I was set before my older brother Manasseh.
I was Joseph's younger son.
I was a daughter of Levi.
I hid my baby son for three months.
I made an ark of bulrushes and daubed it with slime and pitch.
Pharaoh's daughter paid me to nurse my own son.
I was the mother of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.
I was one of seven daughters of a priest of Midian.
A stranger helped us water our flock when shepherds drove us away.
I bore a son named Gershom.
I circumcised my son with a sharp stone on the way to Egypt.
I was the wife of Moses.
I was a Levite, the son of Izhar.
I gathered 250 princes of the assembly against Moses and Aaron.
I told Moses and Aaron, "Ye take too much upon you."
Moses told me to bring censers before the LORD.
The earth opened and swallowed me and my company.
I was of the tribe of Judah.
I coveted a goodly Babylonish garment.
I hid silver and gold in the earth under my tent.
Because of my sin, Israel was defeated at Ai.
I was stoned in the valley of Achor.
I was one of Aaron's sons.
My father's garments were put on me on mount Hor.
I ministered in the priest's office in my father's stead.
I divided the land of Canaan with Joshua.
I was the high priest who succeeded Aaron.
My grandfather was Aaron.
I was zealous for my God when Israel sinned at Peor.
I thrust a javelin through an Israelite man and a Midianite woman.
God gave me his covenant of peace.
I was the son of Eleazar the priest.
I went up the hill with Moses during the battle with Amalek.
With Aaron I held up Moses' hands until the going down of the sun.
Aaron and I were left in charge while Moses went up the mount.
My grandson Bezaleel was filled with the spirit of God for craftsmanship.
I held up one of Moses' hands while Aaron held the other.
I was the son of Zippor.
I was king of the Moabites.
I was distressed because Israel was so many.
I sent princes to bring a prophet to curse Israel.
I built seven altars, but the prophet I hired blessed Israel instead.
I was of the tribe of Judah, the son of Uri.
God filled me with his spirit in wisdom and understanding.
I worked in gold, silver and brass, and in cutting of stones.
Aholiab worked alongside me.
I made the ark of shittim wood.
I was king of Bashan.
I was one of the remnant of the giants.
My bedstead was of iron, nine cubits long.
I came out against Israel to battle at Edrei.
Israel took sixty of my cities.
I was captain of Jabin's army.
I had nine hundred chariots of iron.
My army was routed by Barak at the river Kishon.
I fled on foot to the tent of Heber the Kenite.
A woman drove a nail through my temples.
My father promised me as wife to whoever took Kirjathsepher.
Othniel won my hand.
I asked my father for a blessing.
I asked for springs of water because I had been given a south land.
I was Caleb's daughter.
I was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
I invited a fleeing captain into my tent.
He asked for water, and I gave him milk.
Deborah's song called me blessed above women in the tent.
I killed Sisera with a tent nail.
I was a man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites.
My wife was barren until an angel appeared to her.
I prayed that the man of God would come again and teach us.
The angel ascended in the flame of our altar.
I was the father of Samson.
I lived in the valley of Sorek.
The Philistine lords each offered me eleven hundred pieces of silver.
I bound a man with green withs and new ropes.
I wove his seven locks into the web.
Samson told me his secret, and I had his head shaved while he slept.
My father was Jerubbaal.
I killed seventy of my brothers upon one stone.
My youngest brother Jotham escaped and told a parable of the trees.
The men of Shechem made me king.
A woman cast a piece of millstone upon my head at Thebez.
I was a man of Ramathaimzophim, of mount Ephraim.
I had two wives.
I gave a worthy portion to the wife I loved.
I asked my wife, "Am not I better to thee than ten sons?"
I was Hannah's husband and the father of Samuel.
I was a woman of Moab.
I married one of Naomi's sons.
My husband and his brother both died.
I wept and kissed my mother-in-law goodbye.
I went back to my people while my sister-in-law Ruth stayed.
I was king of the Amalekites.
Saul spared me against God's command.
I came delicately, thinking the bitterness of death was past.
Samuel hewed me in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal.
Sparing me helped cost Saul his kingdom.
I was a champion of the Philistines from Gath.
My height was six cubits and a span.
The staff of my spear was like a weaver's beam.
I defied the armies of Israel for forty days.
A shepherd boy killed me with a sling and a stone.
I was an Edomite.
I was the chiefest of Saul's herdmen.
I saw David receive bread and a sword at Nob.
I reported Ahimelech the priest to Saul.
When others refused, I killed eighty-five priests.
I was captain of Saul's host.
I made Ishbosheth king over Israel.
I killed Asahel with the end of my spear.
I made a league with David at Hebron.
Joab killed me in the gate of Hebron.
My mother was Zeruiah, David's sister.
I went up first against the Jebusites and so became chief.
I killed Abner to avenge my brother Asahel.
I thrust three darts through Absalom's heart.
I was captain of David's army; Benaiah killed me by the altar.
I was a son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab.
I went with David by night into Saul's camp.
I wanted to smite Saul to the earth with his own spear.
I asked to take off the head of Shimei, who cursed David.
I rescued David from the giant Ishbibenob.
I was a son of Zeruiah.
I was as light of foot as a wild roe.
I pursued Abner and would not turn aside.
I was one of David's thirty mighty men.
Abner killed me with the hinder end of his spear.
I was a woman of good understanding and beautiful countenance.
My husband was churlish and evil in his doings.
I brought two hundred loaves and five sheep to meet an army.
I kept David from avenging himself with his own hand.
After my husband Nabal died, I became David's wife.
I had three thousand sheep and a thousand goats.
I was of the house of Caleb.
I asked, "Who is David?" and turned his young men away.
My name means fool, and folly was with me.
My heart died within me and I became as a stone.
My nurse fled with me in haste; I fell and became lame.
I lived in Lodebar, in the house of Machir.
I called myself a dead dog before the king.
I ate continually at the king's table.
I was Jonathan's son, shown kindness by David.
I was an Archite.
I met David with my coat rent and earth upon my head.
David sent me back to defeat the counsel of Ahithophel.
Absalom chose my counsel over Ahithophel's.
I was known as David's friend.
I carried the ark of the covenant when David fled Jerusalem.
David told me to carry the ark back into the city.
My son Ahimaaz ran to bring David tidings.
I anointed Solomon king at Gihon.
Solomon put me in the room of Abiathar as priest.
I was the son of Jehoiada.
I slew a lion in a pit in time of snow.
I killed an Egyptian with his own spear.
I was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites.
Solomon made me captain of the host in Joab's place.
I was the son of Haggith.
I exalted myself, saying, "I will be king."
I prepared chariots and fifty men to run before me.
I caught hold of the horns of the altar in fear of Solomon.
I asked for Abishag the Shunammite as my wife and was put to death.
I was the son of Solomon.
I forsook the counsel of the old men.
I followed the young men's advice and answered the people roughly.
Ten tribes rebelled against me.
Shishak king of Egypt took the treasures of the temple in my reign.
I was Solomon's servant, an Ephrathite.
A prophet tore his new garment into twelve pieces and gave me ten.
I fled from Solomon into Egypt.
I set up golden calves in Bethel and Dan.
My hand dried up when I put it forth against a man of God.
I was the son of Omri.
I married Jezebel and served Baal.
I called Elijah the one that troubled Israel.
I lay on my bed and would eat no bread because I wanted a vineyard.
An arrow drawn at a venture struck me between the joints of the harness.
I was a Jezreelite.
My vineyard was hard by the king's palace.
I refused to give the king the inheritance of my fathers.
Two false witnesses said I blasphemed God and the king.
Jezebel had me stoned so that Ahab could take my vineyard.
I was king of Judah, the son of Asa.
I joined Ahab in battle at Ramothgilead.
I cried out when enemy captains mistook me for the king of Israel.
I sent Levites to teach the book of the law in the cities of Judah.
My army sang praises, and the LORD set ambushments against our enemies.
I was hidden in the house of the LORD for six years.
My aunt Jehosheba stole me away from among the king's sons who were slain.
I began to reign when I was seven years old.
I set a chest with a hole in its lid to collect money for repairing the temple.
I did right all the days that Jehoiada the priest instructed me.
I was a priest in the days of Athaliah.
My wife hid the king's son from Athaliah.
I brought forth the king's son and put the crown upon him.
I commanded that Athaliah be slain outside the house of the LORD.
I died at a hundred and thirty years old and was buried among the kings.
I became king of Judah at sixteen years old.
I sought God in the days of Zechariah.
I loved husbandry and built towers in the desert.
My heart was lifted up and I went into the temple to burn incense.
Leprosy rose up in my forehead; Isaiah saw the Lord in the year I died.
I began to reign when I was twelve years old.
I reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem.
I built altars for all the host of heaven in the house of the LORD.
The Assyrians took me among the thorns, bound me with fetters, and carried me to Babylon.
I humbled myself in my affliction, and God brought me back to Jerusalem.
I was king of Tyre.
I sent cedar trees, carpenters and masons to build David a house.
I was ever a lover of David.
I supplied Solomon with cedar and fir trees for the temple.
Solomon gave me twenty cities in Galilee, and they pleased me not.
I was king of Babylon.
I carried vessels of the house of God to the house of my god.
I dreamed of a great image whose head was of fine gold.
I cast three men into a burning fiery furnace.
I ate grass as oxen until I knew that the most High ruleth.
I made a great feast to a thousand of my lords.
We drank wine from the golden vessels taken from Jerusalem.
I saw the fingers of a man's hand writing upon the wall.
My knees smote one against another.
I was slain the same night the writing was interpreted.
I took the kingdom being about threescore and two years old.
I set a hundred and twenty princes over the kingdom.
I signed a decree that no one could ask a petition of anyone but me for thirty days.
I passed the night fasting, and my sleep went from me.
I rose very early and went in haste to the den of lions.
Isaiah's prophecy named me as God's shepherd.
God called me his anointed, whose right hand he had holden.
I was king of Persia.
The LORD stirred up my spirit to make a proclamation.
I proclaimed that the house of God at Jerusalem should be rebuilt.
I was the son of Shealtiel.
I led the first company of returning exiles with Jeshua.
My hands laid the foundation of the house of God.
The word came to me: "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit."
I was governor of Judah in the days of Haggai.
I prophesied in the second year of Darius the king.
I asked whether it was time to dwell in ceiled houses while God's house lay waste.
I said they earned wages to put into a bag with holes.
I said the glory of the latter house would be greater than the former.
I prophesied with Zechariah to stir up the rebuilding of the temple.
I was the son of Berechiah.
I saw a man riding on a red horse among the myrtle trees.
I saw a candlestick all of gold and two olive trees.
I foretold a king coming lowly, riding upon an ass.
I wrote of thirty pieces of silver cast to the potter.
I was the son of Pethuel.
I described a land stripped by the palmerworm, locust and cankerworm.
I called the people to rend their heart, and not their garments.
I foretold that God would pour out his spirit upon all flesh.
Peter quoted my prophecy on the day of Pentecost.
I was among the herdmen of Tekoa.
I said I was no prophet, but a gatherer of sycomore fruit.
I saw the Lord standing with a plumbline in his hand.
I was shown a basket of summer fruit.
I said, "Let judgment run down as waters."
I was the son of Beeri.
The LORD told me to take a wife of whoredoms.
My wife was Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim.
I named my children Loruhamah and Loammi.
I bought my wife back for fifteen pieces of silver.
I was of the daughters of Aaron.
I was barren, and well stricken in years.
My babe leaped in my womb at Mary's greeting.
I asked, "Whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?"
I was the mother of John the Baptist.
I was a priest of the course of Abia.
An angel appeared to me by the altar of incense.
I was struck dumb because I believed not the angel's words.
I wrote on a writing table, "His name is John."
Filled with the Holy Ghost, I prophesied, "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel."
I was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel.
It was revealed that I would not see death before I had seen the Lord's Christ.
I came by the Spirit into the temple.
I took the child Jesus up in my arms and blessed God.
I said, "Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace."
I was a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel.
I was of the tribe of Aser.
I had lived with a husband seven years from my virginity.
I departed not from the temple, serving God with fastings and prayers night and day.
I spoke of the child Jesus to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem.
I was one of the rulers of the synagogue.
I fell at Jesus' feet and begged him to come to my house.
My only daughter was about twelve years of age.
Messengers came to tell me, "Thy daughter is dead."
Jesus took my daughter by the hand and said, "Talitha cumi."
I was the son of Timaeus.
I sat by the highway side begging near Jericho.
I cried out, "Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me."
I cast away my garment and came to Jesus.
I was blind, and Jesus said, "Thy faith hath made thee whole."
I was governor of Judaea.
I asked, "What is truth?"
My wife sent word to have nothing to do with that just man.
I washed my hands before the multitude.
I wrote the title "JESUS OF NAZARETH THE KING OF THE JEWS."
I was the high priest that same year.
I said it was expedient that one man should die for the people.
The chief priests assembled in my palace to plot.
Annas was my father-in-law.
I rent my clothes, saying, "He hath spoken blasphemy."
I was a notable prisoner.
I had committed murder in an insurrection.
John's Gospel calls me a robber.
The crowd chose me to be released.
I was set free, and Jesus was delivered to be crucified.
I was an honourable counsellor.
I had not consented to the council's counsel and deed.
I was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly for fear of the Jews.
I went in boldly unto Pilate and craved the body of Jesus.
I laid Jesus in my own new tomb, hewn out in the rock.
I was coming out of the country into Jerusalem.
I was the father of Alexander and Rufus.
Soldiers compelled me to do a task.
I bore the cross after Jesus.
I am remembered as the man of Cyrene who carried Jesus' cross.
I was a centurion of the band called the Italian band.
I was devout and gave much alms to the people.
An angel told me to send men to Joppa for Peter.
I fell down at Peter's feet and worshipped him.
The Holy Ghost fell on my household while Peter was still speaking.
I was a seller of purple.
I came from the city of Thyatira.
I heard Paul by a riverside at Philippi.
The Lord opened my heart.
I was baptized with my household and constrained Paul to stay at my house.
I was a disciple at Joppa.
I was full of good works and almsdeeds.
Widows showed the coats and garments I had made.
Peter knelt down, prayed, and told me to arise.
I am the woman Peter raised from the dead at Joppa.
I was a disciple at Damascus.
The Lord told me to go into the street called Straight.
I protested that I had heard how much evil this man had done.
I put my hands on Saul so that he might receive his sight.
Paul later described me as a devout man according to the law.
My husband and I sold a possession.
We kept back part of the price.
Peter asked me whether the land was sold for so much.
We agreed together to tempt the Spirit of the Lord.
I fell down dead at Peter's feet, just as my husband had.
I was a damsel in the house of Mary, the mother of John Mark.
I came to answer a knock at the door of the gate.
I knew Peter's voice.
For gladness I did not open the gate.
They said I was mad, but I constantly affirmed it was so.
I was a young man at Troas.
I sat in a window while Paul preached long.
I sank down with a deep sleep.
I fell down from the third loft and was taken up dead.
Paul embraced me and said, "His life is in him."
Many gathered to pray at my mother Mary's house.
I went with Barnabas and Saul as their minister.
I departed from them at Pamphylia and returned to Jerusalem.
Paul and Barnabas parted company over whether to take me.
Paul later wrote that I was profitable to him for the ministry.
I was a Pharisee and a doctor of the law.
I was had in reputation among all the people.
I advised the council to refrain from the apostles and let them alone.
I said that if the work was of God, they could not overthrow it.
Paul was brought up at my feet.
I was governor when Paul was sent to me at Caesarea.
Tertullus the orator accused Paul before me.
My wife Drusilla was a Jewess.
I trembled as Paul reasoned of righteousness, temperance and judgment.
I hoped Paul would give me money, and I left him bound for two years.
I came into my province after Felix.
Paul appealed unto Caesar before me.
I told King Agrippa about Paul's case.
I said with a loud voice, "Paul, thou art beside thyself."
I said much learning had made Paul mad.
I came to Caesarea with Bernice to salute Festus.
I said, "I would also hear the man myself."
Paul thought himself happy to answer for himself before me.
I said, "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian."
I said Paul might have been set at liberty if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
I was the deputy of the country at Paphos.
I was described as a prudent man.
I called for Barnabas and Saul, wanting to hear the word of God.
A sorcerer tried to turn me away from the faith.
I believed, astonished at the doctrine of the Lord.
I was a sorcerer and false prophet, a Jew.
I was also known as Barjesus.
I was with the deputy of the country.
Paul called me a child of the devil.
I was struck blind for a season.
Paul sent greetings from me to the Colossians, along with Luke.
Paul called me one of his fellowlabourers.
I sent greetings to Philemon along with Mark, Aristarchus and Luke.
I loved this present world.
I forsook Paul and departed unto Thessalonica.
I was a prophet who came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
I signified by the Spirit that there would be a great dearth throughout all the world.
My prophecy came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar.
I came down from Judaea to Caesarea.
I bound my own hands and feet with Paul's girdle.
I am named only once in Scripture.
Paul remembered my unfeigned faith.
My daughter was Eunice.
Faith dwelt first in me.
I was Timothy's grandmother.
I had been the wife of Philip, then married his brother Herod.
John the Baptist said it was not lawful for Herod to have me.
I had a quarrel against John and would have killed him.
My daughter danced before Herod on his birthday.
I told my daughter to ask for John the Baptist's head in a charger.
My husband Chuza was Herod's steward.
I had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities.
I ministered unto Jesus of my substance.
I came to the sepulchre with spices on the first day of the week.
I told the apostles about the empty tomb, with Mary Magdalene.
